reforms.description: The government actively promotes private initiatives through provisions in the tax code, including a tax credit for research and experimentation expenditures, to catalyze the development and diffusion of technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The tax credit incentivizes private sector investment in R&D, which can lead to increased innovation and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: The tax credit has been actively utilized by firms since its introduction.
reforms.importance_rationale: While not a major overhaul, the tax credit represents a significant policy tool to encourage R&D investment.
reforms.source_quote: Research and experimentation (R&E) expenditures can be expensed and increases in R&E expenditures are subject to a tax credit of 20 per cent of qualified expenditures over a base amount.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions a 'tax credit for research and experimentation expenditures' which directly relates to innovation instruments for firms.

reforms.description: The government promotes private initiatives through tax provisions and partnerships with industry to develop and diffuse technology, including a tax credit for research and experimentation expenditures. Additionally, the Advanced Technology Program facilitates industry-led partnerships to share costs for developing high-risk advanced technologies that private firms would not otherwise undertake, while the Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) has expanded its network of technology extension centres to help small and medium-sized enterprises adopt appropriate manufacturing technologies.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: These initiatives are designed to enhance technological development and adoption, which supports economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: All programs mentioned are stated to be implemented.
reforms.importance_rationale: These reforms significantly enhance the support for innovation but do not represent a structural overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: The Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP), which links universities, communities, and government through a nation-wide network of technology extension centres to help SMEs adopt appropriate manufacturing technologies, has expanded from 7 to 44 centres.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description includes 'tax provisions and partnerships with industry to develop and diffuse technology' and mentions a 'tax credit for research and experimentation expenditures', indicating a strong focus on innovation instruments.
